players.product: data-center air-cooled & water-cooled chillers, CDUs (1.3 MW / 2.5 MW / 5 MW) and Nlyte DCIM

quarterly_data.signal: Fort Worth chiller plant: Carrier plans to invest more than $600 million over the next three years in a new advanced manufacturing and engineering center of more than 1 million square feet in Fort Worth, Texas, expanding U.S. capacity for commercial chillers (air- and water-cooled) and other advanced thermal management systems; operations are expected to begin in 2027, creating 1,500 jobs. Carrier says the investment supports record backlog levels in its commercial HVAC business driven by strong demand across data centers, healthcare, education, industrial markets and other verticals (no backlog figure given). CEO David Gitlin: 'This investment reflects the strong demand we are securing for high-performance, energy-efficient solutions.'
quarterly_data.figure: more than $600 million over three years; operations from 2027
